text:
maria: Hey team, escalated from ACME app — they see intermittent RuntimeError + connection resets when calling our Python sync SDK from FastAPI background threads. High error rate under concurrency.

kevin: Can you paste the minimal repro and the stack trace? Also which redwood and httpx versions?

maria: Repro is a small FastAPI service using ThreadPoolExecutor for long-running sync work. They call our sync wrapper from inside a background thread.

maria: stack trace (sanitized):
```
RuntimeError: This event loop is already running
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/sync_wrapper.py", line 42, in request
    return asyncio.run(self._async_request(...))
  File "/usr/lib/python3.10/asyncio/runners.py", line 44, in run
    loop.run_until_complete(task)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.10/asyncio/base_events.py", line 604, in run_until_complete
    raise RuntimeError('This event loop is already running')
```

maria: Versions from customer: redwood-py 0.12.0, httpx 0.23.0, FastAPI 0.95.0, uvicorn 0.21.1, Python 3.10. Concurrency: gunicorn with 4 workers, threads=10, using ThreadPoolExecutor for background tasks.

kevin: Looks like our sync wrapper calls asyncio.run internally which fails when invoked inside an already-running loop (common with uvicorn's loop and some thread contexts). httpx 0.23 had some behavior around AsyncClient that interacts badly with threaded sync wrappers.

kevin: Quick checks: 1) Do calls from the main request handler (no thread) succeed? 2) Can customer try switching to async usage (await client.async_client.call(...)) instead of sync wrapper inside thread?

maria: Main request path tends to be fine. The failures spike when they offload work to a background threadpool. They can't easily refactor to fully async yet. They asked for a compatible fix without rewriting major app logic.

samir: For interim workaround: run sync calls in a fresh process or use anyio.to_thread.run_sync to ensure no nested loop collisions. Example pattern: 
```py
from anyio import to_thread

def sync_task(payload):
    from redwood import RedwoodSyncClient
    c = RedwoodSyncClient(...)
    return c.complete(payload)

# in async handler
await to_thread.run_sync(sync_task, payload)
```
This avoids asyncio.run inside an already running loop.

maria: Customer tried to_thread.run_sync and error rate dropped to ~0.5%. Good short-term.

kevin: Long term, recommend: 1) upgrade redwood-py to 0.13.2 (we changed sync wrapper to use loop.run_in_executor instead of asyncio.run), 2) upgrade httpx to 0.24.1 which contains relevant fixes, 3) if possible prefer AsyncClient usage in an async codepath.

maria: I can confirm customer upgraded to redwood-py 0.13.2 + httpx 0.24.1 and their error rate went to 0.1% (mostly unrelated network flakes). They rolled the patch to prod.

kevin: Share a short note for support playbook so CS can triage quickly:
- If errors show "This event loop is already running" or "Event loop is closed" when using the sync SDK from FastAPI/uvicorn threads, ask for: redwood-py and httpx versions, deployment (gunicorn/uvicorn), and whether calls run inside threads/processes.
- Short-term: suggest anyio.to_thread.run_sync or offload to separate process.
- Medium-term: upgrade to redwood-py >= 0.13.2 and httpx >= 0.24.1.

samir: I'll add a snippet to the KB and a one-line check you can paste in support replies to validate version combo.

samir: paste-in-check: 
```bash
python -c "import redwood, httpx, sys; print(redwood.__version__, httpx.__version__, sys.version)"
```

maria: Thanks — customer is happy. Marking resolved. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Incident 3421: customer fix deployed to prod (redwood-py 0.13.2) at 2056781270 UTC

kevin: Nice work. I'll follow up with a small SDK doc update to make the compat guidance clearer.

maria: filing a support template now, linking the KB snippet and the repro used by ACME.

kevin: thumbs up.
